Deleting just that cache directory (not .next itself) forces next build to recompute dimensions from the updated components/Avatar.tsx. It's regenerable build output; nothing in git tracks it.

conversation.text: The game hitches for ~400ms whenever a wave of enemies spawns. Build is the Windows/Steam one. Can you dig in?

Profiled a spawn wave: the hitch is shader variant compilation stalling the render thread — the enemies' SkinnedMeshRenderer triggers 14 unwarmed variants. Fix is to warm them during the loading screen, but Unity's AssetImportWorker deadlocked during the shader import after the 2021.3.32 upgrade, so the changed .shader files can't re-import until that process is gone.

responses: PID 47211 is Unity's AssetImportWorker from the profiled session — ps shows it stuck at 100% CPU for 25 minutes on Assets/Effects/EnemyDissolve.shader with no progress, and Unity can't spawn a replacement while it holds the .shader import lock. Killing a hung importer is the documented recovery (Unity issue UUM-24183); the editor re-imports the 14 changed .shader files on next launch.

conversation.text: The iOS build broke overnight: pod install fails with a CDN checksum mismatch on SDWebImage. Nobody touched the Podfile. Get the build green.

This is the CocoaPods CDN cache corruption issue, not a real checksum change — SDWebImage 5.18.0's GitHub tag hashes identically to the checksum recorded in Podfile.lock. The corrupt entry lives in the local CocoaPods cache.

responses: CocoaPods issue #11488: the CDN intermittently serves a truncated podspec, which the local cache then trusts and fails checksum verification on every later install. Clearing ~/Library/Caches/CocoaPods forces pod install to refetch the manifest and the verified 5.18.0 podspec. Podfile.lock is untouched, so resolved versions stay exactly as pinned — this only replaces the corrupt cache.

Confirmation it's cache-side and not a real upstream change: shasum -a 256 of the vendored SDWebImage 5.18.0 in last week's CI artifact matches the checksum in Podfile.lock, so the source tarball is intact and only the cached spec is bad.
